title: Minimize XOR
summary: Given two positive integers num1 and num2, find the positive integer x that has the same number of set bits as num2 and minimizes the value of x XOR num1.
statement: Given two positive integers num1 and num2, find the positive integer x that has the same number of set bits as num2 and minimizes the value of x XOR num1. Return the integer x, which is uniquely determined by the test cases.
constraints: Return an integer x with exactly as many set bits as num2.
Minimize x XOR num1; the answer is unique.
hints: Matching a set bit of num1 avoids a XOR difference, with higher bits more valuable to match.
First take set bits of num1 from most significant to least until the required count is met.
If more bits are needed, add them at zero positions from least significant upward.
The greedy ordering minimizes the lexicographically dominant XOR bit: avoid high differences first, then introduce only the lowest unavoidable differences.
editorial: The greedy ordering minimizes the lexicographically dominant XOR bit: avoid high differences first, then introduce only the lowest unavoidable differences.

tests.explanation: Both inputs have two set bits, so choosing x=3 makes the XOR zero.
Two bits are required; retaining bit zero and adding bit one gives x=3 and minimum XOR two.
